differences: Trial-level mean compensation on down-shift trials is 2.96 mel in the shared table; the paper reports 2.69 (probably transposed digits; the up-shift mean, -3.99, matches).

The paper's compensation model with random intercepts for participant and study gives -6.96 here (statsmodels); the reported -6.93 is matched by the participant-only model used as the check, as if lme4 estimated the study variance at zero. The one-shot model with both intercepts matches (-2.14).

SEs not reproduced: shift magnitude in the trial-level relationship model 3.39 (paper 3.34); participant-level relationship 0.059 (paper 0.058). The trial-level SEs of the condition means (0.26-0.33) are not plain SEs of the rows and were not reproduced.
Cohen's d against 0 for up shifts: 0.45 for compensation (paper 0.49) and 0.40 for one-shot adaptation (paper 0.38), with the formula that reproduces the paper's other d values.

The paper counts 91 people, 40 of them in both Niziolek & Parrell 2021 sessions; the shared table has 92 participant codes, 39 in both sessions and one only in each, so one person probably carries two codes.
